summary: A minimalist bluffing and deduction game where each turn you play one of just two cards in hand, using character powers to guess, compare, or eliminate opponents. Rounds are over in minutes, and the tension comes almost entirely from reading what little information is available about who holds what.
praised: extremely fast to teach and play
surprisingly tense bluffing and deduction from a tiny card pool
great icebreaker or filler between heavier games
scales well from two players up to larger groups
criticised: outcomes can feel very swingy and luck-driven, especially in short rounds
player elimination within a round can leave someone waiting
limited strategic depth for players wanting a serious game

interaction.detail: Almost every card played targets another specific player, forcing guesses, comparisons, or eliminations, so the entire game state is about what your opponents might be holding rather than any private tableau. There is essentially no solitaire play — every turn is about the other players.

scoring.how_you_win: Each round ends by elimination or deck exhaustion, and the last player standing (or holder of the highest card) takes a favor token; the first player to collect the target number of tokens (set by player count) wins the match.
